description: Blank sex is treated as unknown and its group is not reported.

a.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), compute for each patient (by ID and sex) the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `IGA` − `IGM` per record, ignoring missing values. Also compute the mean of that IGA−IGM average across all patients, and divide each patient's IGA−IGM average by this overall mean. Then break the patients down by sex, leaving out patients whose `SEX` is blank (an empty string), since their sex is unknown. For each sex, report the sex, the average of the patients' average PT, the average of their IGA−IGM averages, and the average of their ratios to the overall mean.
a.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.IGA - l.IGM) AS avg_iga_minus_igm FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), patient_ratios AS (SELECT ID, SEX, avg_pt, avg_iga_minus_igm, avg_iga_minus_igm / AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) OVER () AS ratio FROM patient_averages) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS average_patient_avg_pt, AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) AS average_patient_avg_iga_minus_igm, AVG(ratio) AS average_ratio FROM patient_ratios WHERE SEX <> '' GROUP BY SEX;

b.request: Report each patient with at least one matching laboratory record, grouped by patient ID and sex, with average PT and average per-record IGA−IGM difference, each ignoring null values. Calculate each patient’s ratio as their average IGA−IGM difference divided by the unweighted mean of those patient averages across all patients. Then report, for each nonblank sex, the unweighted averages across its patients of average PT, average IGA−IGM difference, and patient ratio; omit the blank-sex group
b.sql:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt,
        AVG(CASE WHEN l.IGA IS NOT NULL AND l.IGM IS NOT NULL THEN l.IGA - l.IGM END) AS avg_iga_igm_diff
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
patient_ratios AS (
    SELECT
        ID,
        SEX,
        avg_pt,
        avg_iga_igm_diff,
        avg_iga_igm_diff / NULLIF(AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) OVER (), 0) AS patient_ratio
    FROM patient_averages
)
SELECT
    SEX,
    AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_patient_pt,
    AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) AS avg_patient_iga_igm_diff,
    AVG(patient_ratio) AS avg_patient_ratio
FROM patient_ratios
WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(SEX) <> ''
GROUP BY SEX;

c.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), work out each patient's (by ID and sex) average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average `IGA` − `IGM` difference per record, ignoring missing values. Also work out how each patient's IGA−IGM average compares to the mean across all patients, as their average divided by that mean. Then break this down by sex: for each sex, give the average PT, the average IGA−IGM difference, and the average ratio to the overall mean. Blank sex is treated as unknown and its group is not reported.
c.sql:
WITH matched_labs AS (
  SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, l.PT, l.IGA, l.IGM
  FROM Laboratory AS l
  JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
), patient_avgs AS (
  SELECT ID, SEX,
         AVG(PT) AS avg_pt,
         AVG(IGA - IGM) AS avg_iga_igm
  FROM matched_labs
  GROUP BY ID, SEX
), overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_iga_igm) AS mean_patient_diff
  FROM patient_avgs
)
SELECT 'patient' AS row_type,
       pa.ID,
       pa.SEX,
       pa.avg_pt AS average_pt,
       pa.avg_iga_igm AS average_iga_igm_difference,
       pa.avg_iga_igm / NULLIF(om.mean_patient_diff, 0) AS ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM patient_avgs AS pa
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS om
UNION ALL
SELECT 'sex' AS row_type,
       NULL AS ID,
       pa.SEX,
       AVG(pa.avg_pt) AS average_pt,
       AVG(pa.avg_iga_igm) AS average_iga_igm_difference,
       AVG(pa.avg_iga_igm / NULLIF(om.mean_patient_diff, 0)) AS ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM patient_avgs AS pa
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS om
WHERE pa.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(pa.SEX) <> ''
GROUP BY pa.SEX

d.request: When matching laboratory records to patients by `ID` and dropping records with no matching patient, calculate for each patient (by `ID` and sex) the average `PT` and average per-record `IGA − IGM` difference, ignoring missing values. For each patient, also calculate the ratio of their average `IGA − IGM` difference to the mean of that average across all patients. Then report, by sex, the average `PT`, average `IGA − IGM` difference, and average ratio to the overall mean. Treat blank sex as unknown and omit that group from the sex breakdown.
d.sql:
WITH per_patient AS (
  SELECT l.ID,
         p.SEX,
         AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt,
         AVG(CASE WHEN l.IGA IS NOT NULL AND l.IGM IS NOT NULL
                  THEN l.IGA - l.IGM END) AS avg_iga_igm_diff
  FROM Laboratory AS l
  JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID
  GROUP BY l.ID, p.SEX
),
with_ratio AS (
  SELECT ID,
         SEX,
         avg_pt,
         avg_iga_igm_diff,
         avg_iga_igm_diff / NULLIF(AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) OVER (), 0) AS ratio_to_overall_mean
  FROM per_patient
)
SELECT SEX,
       AVG(avg_pt) AS average_pt,
       AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) AS average_iga_igm_difference,
       AVG(ratio_to_overall_mean) AS average_ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM with_ratio
WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(SEX) <> ''
GROUP BY SEX;
